name: shell
description: Run shell commands in the working directory.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Run a shell command in the workspace. The shell is sandboxed: only the workspace is writable, so put scratch files under $TMPDIR rather than /tmp, and /proc cannot be read, so a browser will not start here. To read a web page, use web_fetch or web_browse instead of running a browser from the shell. Installed: curl, wget, python3, perl, jq, unzip, file, pdftotext and pdftoppm (poppler-utils), tesseract with English and German, and python3 with pip, numpy and pillow. There is no root and no apt: a program not installed here comes from the packages tool, and is on PATH from the next call. $HOME is inside the workspace and writable, so `pip install --user <library>` works for a missing Python library and stays in this session. A command may run for up to 15 minutes (timeout_seconds, default 120, at most 900). To wait for something started in the background, wait inside one call — `while kill -0 $PID 2>/dev/null; do sleep 10; done` with timeout_seconds 900 — rather than calling again and again to ask whether it has finished.
